summary: ScreenHeader splits NAV_TABS into plain links plus one standout pill at the nav's end (pill-interactive base, ink-strength override, accent when active, focus-ring), capped at six. TabBar marks its standout ink-strength at rest, matching DS TabBar.jsx's overflow math. Both close the T362 risk: the standout reads active on its own door route OR any MANAGE_GROUP_TABS member (guests/milestones/config), never a hand-copied list. Verified via 16 new unit tests (588->602) plus a temporary Playwright run at mobile/--bp-lg. Found, out of scope: nav.manage has no i18n string yet (T365).

acceptance.criterion: ds fidelity clean for AppHeader/TabBar mirrors
acceptance.evidence: pnpm lint -> '▶ ds fidelity (pnpm ds:verify)' : 'fidelity: 31/31 clean pairs; 0 drifting values; unported: AccountMenu, AlhambraScene, BrideAtTower, Icon, MotorcycleRider, ProfileCard' — identical before and after this task's changes (AppHeader/TabBar dsHash entries in design-mirror.json untouched; only the mirror .ts/.html/.scss files changed, which the checker diffs against the DS source, not against themselves).

acceptance.criterion: the rendering matches the kit at mobile + --bp-lg
acceptance.evidence: Temporary, uncommitted Playwright spec (e2e/tmp-t363-visual.spec.ts, deleted after use — never part of this commit) signed in as the couple (signInAsCouple from e2e/support/auth.ts) and screenshotted: desktop 1280x900 (>= --bp-lg=900px) on /dashboard (resting pill, DS AppHeader.jsx outlined-pill-at-end-of-nav anatomy), /guests (pill accent-on, own door route), /milestones and /config (pill still accent-on via group membership, not its own route — confirms the T362 risk is closed); mobile 390x844 on /dashboard (Manage tab last, ink-strength per TabBar.prompt.md, dot with ink-colored ring) and /milestones (Manage tab accent-on via group membership). `npx playwright test e2e/tmp-t363-visual.spec.ts --project="Desktop Chrome"`: '1 passed (7.4s)' — every waitForSelector('.standout'/'.standout.on'/'.tab.standout'/'.tab.standout.on') resolved, i.e. the DOM state the screenshots show was asserted, not just eyeballed.

acceptance.criterion: keyboard focus ring on the standout pill (focus-ring recipe)
acceptance.evidence: src/app/shared/screen-header/screen-header.scss:86-88 — '.standout:focus-visible { @include r.focus-ring; }', the generated mixin (src/styles/_recipes.scss:49-52: outline 2px solid var(--brand-accent), outline-offset 2px) — no hand-typed outline value. Same temporary Playwright run: standout.focus() on /dashboard produced a visible 2px accent outline around the pill in the screenshot (header-desktop-focus.png, reviewed, not committed).

out_of_scope_touched.why: Not edited by hand. pnpm build (this task's own required verification command) runs scripts/generate-release.mjs, which unconditionally overwrites this file with the current git commit hash — the same mechanic T362's report already documented. The file was already listed as the user's uncommitted work before this task started; left exactly as the build produced it, not staged, not committed, not reverted.

risks.risk: `nav.manage` has no es/en/fr translation yet. Confirmed live during this task's visual check: signed in as the couple, both ScreenHeader's pill and TabBar's tab render the literal untranslated key text 'nav.manage' instead of a real word (public/i18n/{en,es,fr}.json's top-level `nav` block has no `manage` entry — grepped directly). This is not a regression from this task and is already T365's explicit scope ('nav.manage ... in es/en/fr'), so it was not fixed here, but it is a real, currently-live gap rather than a hypothetical one.
risks.surfaces_at: T365, and any manual/browser check of the couple's nav taken before T365 lands.

risks.risk: ScreenHeader's six-item cap (MAX_HEADER_ITEMS, screen-header.ts) is implemented defensively per DS AppHeader's ceiling but has no dedicated unit test proving the slice, because NAV_TABS is a real module-level singleton derived from the live route tree (today's couple surface is 4 tabs, well under 6) and this repo has no existing precedent for mocking that module in a spec. If a future task grows a role's primary surface past six destinations, add a test that exercises the cap directly rather than trusting the live route count to stay small.
risks.surfaces_at: Any future task adding a nav destination to a role that already has 5+ entries.
